title: Feature Friction Lab — iterative feature-factory notes
body:
Purpose / context:
I want a lightweight playground for trying out small, composable response-economy features we can ship behind flags. The goal is not a single monolith PRD; this is a personal lab for quickly sketching tradeoffs, user stories, cheap protos, and guardrails that can be cherry-picked and hardened later.

Top-level idea: Feature Factory = small interchangeable feature modules (presets, compactors, micro-filters, tone adapters) that can be combined server-side or at the SDK layer. Each module has: config surface, simple metrics, quick canary recipe, and a fallback plan.

Why this matters now:
- Customers hitting high token spend on chat assistants; need finer-grained levers to reduce unit cost per interaction without killing UX.
- We already have batching/caching/quantization levers; product-side features give more immediate impact to teams who can't change model families.
- Plays nicely with Dedicated & Private (modules can be policy-guarded per deployment).

Quick hypothesis list (to validate):
- H1: Small deterministic compressions pre- or post-model call (e.g., prune backstory lines, strip filler turns) can save 15–30% tokens with <3% user-reported quality loss.
- H2: User-level presets (concise / verbose / technical / friendly) reduce variance and let customers optimize per-user cohort.
- H3: A micro-eval pipeline (cheap human-review on rolling sample) can catch regressions introduced by composition of modules.

Feature seeds (short descriptions):
1) Compact Recap module — post-process responses to produce a 1–3 line summary + optional details link. Config: max_sentences, allow_truncation, preserve_entities. Use case: mobile-first UIs to conserve tokens.

2) Affordance Trimmer — heuristics + tiny model pass that removes low-value assistant chatter before sending back. Config: keep_threshold, allowed_gambits (e.g., clarifying question), preserve_proactive_actions. Fallback: if trimmer would remove >30% of response, return original and flag.

3) Style Presets — server-side profile affecting generation temperature, instruction templates, and post-processing. Presets: concise, developer, legal-safe, empathetic. Exposure: SDK param + user preference in profile.

4) Conditional Fallback Router — if model latency > SLO or token estimate > budget -> route to cheaper model variant + add short prefix explaining behavior.

5) Interaction Stitcher — when conversation contains long quoted blocks (emails, docs), replace quoted content with a compact anchor + 'expand' token to fetch full-on-demand. Saves tokens for typical read/scan patterns.

Metrics to collect (minimum viable):
- token_delta (tokens_before - tokens_after) per module
- user_visible_quality_flag (binary per sampled turn via micro-eval)
- time_to_first_byte / latency impact per module
- activation_rate (how often module made non-zero changes)
- rollback_signals (user re-asks, low satisfaction events)

Example quick experiment plan (Compact Recap):
- Week 0: implement as post-process hook in sandbox (lambda) — naive heuristic + optional GPT-lite summarize.
- Week 1: run on 10% of internal traffic (canary) for 2k daily turns; collect token_delta, latency, and sample 100 turns for raters.
- Week 2: iterate thresholds to hit 20% tokens saved and keeper rate >= 95% for raters.
- Week 3: expand to selected external customers for opt-in beta.

User stories (short):
- As a mobile user, I want short answers so I can read quicker and save data.
- As a PM, I want an opt-in concise preset to measure engagement before rolling it org-wide.
- As a platform engineer, I want modules to be toggled per-customer and have a safe fallback when production behavior trips.

Acceptance criteria (for initial proto):
- Module can be toggled via SDK param and server flag.
- Pipeline records token_delta and latency per invocation.
- 200 sampled turns with blinded raters show <= 5% severe-quality regressions.
- Canary tooling emits alerts when rollback_signals exceed threshold.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Combinatorial interactions between modules create unexpected regressions. Mitigation: enforce composition order, add micro-eval gating when new combos are enabled.
- Risk: Users confused by silent truncation. Mitigation: surface explicit affordance (e.g., "Shortened to save tokens — expand"), allow user override.
- Risk: Performance overhead (extra passes). Mitigation: prioritize cheap heuristics, async post-processing for non-critical paths.

Open questions (to answer in follow-ups):
- Where do we place decisioning? SDK, edge, or core infra? Tradeoffs: SDK easier for per-user UX, core infra easier for centralized metrics and security.
- How do we attribute cost savings back to customer billing/credits?
- Which modules should be allowed on Private deployments without approval?

Next actionable items (my personal TODO):
- Prototype Compact Recap as server-side postprocess (POC branch linked).
- Set up minimal micro-eval form + rotation in prod raters.
- Sketch SDK param surface and flagging API with SRE (cc: Kai).
- Draft short customer-facing one-pager for beta participants (aim: show savings + opt-in flow).

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep feature modules small — target change set < 200 LOC where possible.
- Think of presets as a composition of instruction templates + postprocess hooks.
- Explore heartbeat tags in telemetry to make it trivial to roll back per-customer.
- Maybe tie to Optimize suggestions (we could auto-suggest "enable Compact Recap" for low-engagement mobile cohorts).

Slack crumbs/refs: slack thread #prod-econ Feb 12 about 'short answers' spike; pinged @maya for micro-eval help.

Short brainstorm for names (pick one for the project):
- Feature Forge
- Compact Modules (CM)
- Response Studio
- Friction Lab (current working)

If I circle back later: formalize 1-pager, pick telemetry schema, and write minimal safety checklist for composition.

-- yusuf

(End of scratchpad — this is deliberately terse and messy; copy to shared drive page when ready.)
